messages.subject: Statistical test using normalized spectral counts
messages.subject_clean: Statistical test using normalized spectral counts
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,
I would like to use Msstats to analyze my label free proteomics data. In brief, my goal is to study the difference in the label-free proteome at three time points (0, 1 and 4hr). The data was first processed using MaxQuant. Subsequently, I did normalization and imputation (based on their spectral counts).

In my dataset spectral counts are not integer numbers anymore; I reduced the bias in the number of spectral counts caused by a protein’s length (longer proteins tend to have more tryptic fragments and thus more spectral counts) by normalizing to the protein’s length. I further normalized these data to reduce the variability between samples. Now I want to do statistical tests on this dataset and pick a subset of proteins of interest. I would like to  look at 0hr vs 1hr and 0hr vs 4hrs.

Is Msstats able to provide a way to visualize the results and pick a list of proteins of interest based on normalized spectral counts ? If yes, what is the best way to approach it?
Thanks
HFaz

Hi Meena and Olga,

I have a few of questions relating to James Webber's questions and your answers.

Question 1:
What causes Skyline to put "NA" vs. "0" in the intensity column? Does "NA" mean that an intensity (i.e. transition) is randomly missing, while a "0" means that there isn't an intensity for a particular transition in multiple samples? In other words, would Skyline put "NA" if a transition was sporadically present in some samples and not in others (aka missing at random), while a "0" would be inserted if a transition was not present in certain samples (like in a control sample that doesn't have the measured peptide/transition)? Could you please explain this and define what 'missing a random means?'

Question 2:
I have SRM data that contains "0" intensity values, but does not contain "NA" intensity values. Based on this thread, it seems like I should set summaryMethod="linear" and censoredInt ="0." I tried running MSstats with these commands and got this error message: "Intensity has 0 or negative values. Please check these intensities and change them." Like James Webber, I want to include as much data as possible in my calculations and be able to calculate fold changes between samples, so would this be an instance where I should change "0" to "1?"

Question3:
Do you notice a big difference in results when cutoffCensored="minRun" vs. cutoffCensored="minFeature?"

Thanks for clarifying.

Scott

messages.body_plain:
Hi Scott,

Thank you for your question and message. They also will be helpful for other users.

Answer 1: I will double-check with Skyline team how they distinguish between them. but interpretation part, what I understand easily, '0' in skyline means they know intensity=0, which means a transition was not present in certain sample, however, NA means they don't know even this zero or other value.

Answer 2: in that case, options should be summaryMethod='linear' and censoredInt="0" and skylineReport=TRUE. Then it will take care of zero. (then log2(intensity) will be zero.) but, MSstats keeps original intensity=0 in order to know which is censored zero. If you change 0 to 1, then intensity=1 after all data processing, and MSstats can't detect this value as censored zero. So, 'skylineReport=TRUE' is best. now censoredInt="0" and skylineReport=TRUE should be added together.

Answer 3: Yes, it depends on the datasets. Depending on the dataset, different assumption for minRun or minFeature is suitable.

hope to help.

-Meena

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-Jz5Sw0J0j8Y/VdYtySU60yI/AAAAAAAAAAM/hmLJ5izK-ck/s1600/ChangeCurrentReport.png>

Dear Meena,

thx for your explanations. Unfortunately, I am still unsure, how to apply the new dataProcess() function correctly. I am currently analysing DIA data in skyline using the top5 fragment ions per peptide and scored the resulting transition groups using a trained mProphet model. Only transition groups showing a  q-value < x were integrated (Refine->Reintegrate peaks->only integrate sig. Q-values). The integration results were exported using the skyline custom report in 10 col. format.

Since I applied mProphet scoring as a censoring mechanism (assumption: scores below a certain cut-off indicate unreliable signals below LOD/LOQ of the instrument), I should be using censoredInt="NA"?

The parameter censored cutoffCensored="minFeature" would force MSstats to replace the censored value ("NA") by the smallest value measured for this feature across conditions. What would happen, if all runs for this feature contain NAs? I guess cutoffCensored="minRun" would solve this problem, since it borrows the min signal intensities from another feature (global min), but are there any drawbacks/implications using this strategy?

dataProcess(..., censoredInt="NA") reports an error in case there are any zero values in the input data, presumably because it can not log transform. I therefor replaced all zeros manually by 1. Is this the correct way of doing it? If yes, why is this not done automatically by the dataProcess() function, since I already informed the function which values are censored ("NA")?

The skyline custom reports now contains a column called "Truncated" that marks transitions that have only been partially integrated due to scheduling (the peak area is most likely not fully contained in the RT window used during data import). How is MSstats using this column?

- Are intensities flaged by Truncated
- Used as they are?
- Replaced by some kind of estimate (imputed, the true value must be bigger, but it's unclear how big).
- Removed from the data?

Thx for your help and keep up the great work,
Tobi

messages.body_plain:
Hi Tobi,

I comment in-line below,

-------------------------------

 I am currently analysing DIA data in skyline using the top5 fragment ions per peptide and scored the resulting transition groups using a trained mProphet model. Only transition groups showing a  q-value < x were integrated (Refine->Reintegrate peaks->only integrate sig. Q-values). The integration results were exported using the skyline custom report in 10 col. format.

And here are my questions:

Since I applied mProphet scoring as a censoring mechanism (assumption: scores below a certain cut-off indicate unreliable signals below LOD/LOQ of the instrument), I should be using censoredInt="NA"?

         --> In this case, measurements, which have scores below a certain cut-off mProphet scoring, should be NA and then use 'censoredInt="NA"'

The parameter censored cutoffCensored="minFeature" would force MSstats to replace the censored value ("NA") by the smallest value measured for this feature across conditions. What would happen, if all runs for this feature contain NAs?

         --> If all runs for this feature contain NAs ( for example, there are total 10 MS runs. and for featureA, NA for run1, NA for run2, ... NA for run10), It seems this feature has no information at all and should not contribute. and MSstats doesn't consider this feature. If I understood your example incorrectly, please let me know.

I guess cutoffCensored="minRun" would solve this problem, since it borrows the min signal intensities from another feature (global min), but are there any drawbacks/implications using this strategy?

         --> If I understood correctly above, I think that we should remove this feature, because this feature can't give us any information. For example, in profile plot, there is no even dot for this feature. If we used cutoffCensored="minRun", some min signal intensities are used in model, which give more weight for min intensities. but, I don't want to recommend because it seems to generate one new feature with min values across runs and conditions.

dataProcess(..., censoredInt="NA") reports an error in case there are any zero values in the input data, presumably because it can not log transform. I therefor replaced all zeros manually by 1. Is this the correct way of doing it? If yes, why is this not done automatically by the dataProcess() function, since I already informed the function which values are censored ("NA")?

         --> Use censoredInt="NA" and skylineReport=TRUE, which will keep zero value. Let's talk about the difference censoredInt="NA" and "0"
            the dataset can have both zero and NA. Then
            1) censoredInt="0" : NA values will be NA. zero values will be considered under cutoff value. Easily, here let's say zero value will be 99% of min Feature (or Run).
            2) censoredInt="NA" : zero values still be zero. (with skylineReport=TRUE, log2(intensity) will be zero. and NA values will be considered under cutoff value. (easily, here let's say NA will be 99% min Feature (or Run) among intensities which is not NA and not zero. Therefore, if you replace 0 to 1 in intensity, MSstats will recognize that min feature value will be 1. if you use skylineReport=TRUE, min feature (across values neither NA nor zero) will be higher than 1.

            From skyline output, we expect very few NAs, even there can be many zero. So, for skyline output, censoredInt="0" is suitable.
            and we know that skyline can distinguish zero and NA. so, skylineReport=TRUE can take care of zero. The reason that censoredInt="NA" has warning message about zero is that we cant guarantee for other spectral tool. So, want to give the user about data. If users know the spectral tool they used can distinguish NA and zero and assumptions is also correct, they can use 'skylineReport=TRUE'. It should work.

The skyline custom reports now contains a column called "Truncated" that marks transitions that have only been partially integrated due to scheduling (the peak area is most likely not fully contained in the RT window used during data import). How is MSstats using this column?

- Are intensities flaged by Truncated
- Used as they are?
- Replaced by some kind of estimate (imputed, the true value must be bigger, but it's unclear how big).
- Removed from the data?

          --> use 'skylineReport=TRUE'. Then the intensities with 'Truncated=TRUE' will be replace with NAs, which means to remove these truncated peaks.

--------------------------

hope to help.

-Meena
